"No action" would constitute a reneging of the Department's responsibilities in stewardship of the public lands.
B) Close all Department of the Interior Lands to ORV Use:
This alternative, perhaps the best in terms of protecting the integrity of ecosystems which maintain the character of the public lands, would limit the spectrum of recreation opportunities (present and future) available to the general public and would particularly limit those presently using ORV on the public lands.
Selection of this alternative would result in the following impacts:
There would be more protection afforded all the natural features of landscapes under stewardship of the Department and an attendant reinstatement of some ecosystem interactions which have been disrupted by ORV in the past.
There would be a cessation of ORV effects (such as erosion) on the public lands.
There would be no disturbance of animals and plants on those public land areas where ORV use previously had created such disturbance.
There would be effects on economic sectors which are presently influenced by current demand for and production of ORV. The closing of Interior lands to ORV would in some instances affect the economies of areas near Department lands where ORV use takes place.
Closing all Department of the Interior lands to ORV use would not be consistent with the Department's mandate to provide the broadest possible mix of compatible multiple uses on certain of its lands—multiple uses which include recreation among the primary potentials and ORV use being a primary source of enjoyment to significant numbers of recreationists.
